question: Do the 2014 citation and secondary catalog entries clarify whether the 2010 BAR proceedings citation is a separate source or a citation variant of the NAST abstract?

evidence.citation: Jumawan, Herrera, and Vallejo (2014), reference entry 2010b.
evidence.finding: The article bibliography cites a 2010 Jumawan, Herrera, and Jacinto title variant as a NAST-Philippines Transactions item, volume 32, page 80, and gives 10 July 2010 / Manila. The article copy is author-uploaded; its bibliography is not an independent primary copy of the 2010 work.

evidence.sourceType: secondary bibliographic index; direct page access denied
evidence.citation: CABI Compendium profile reference list, as exposed in indexed search text.
evidence.finding: The indexed excerpt also lists a 2010 Jumawan, Herrera, and Jacinto title variant as NAST Transactions, volume 32, page 80. Direct access to the CABI page returned HTTP 403, so this is recorded as a search-index excerpt only.

evidence.citation: UP Diliman Institute of Environmental Science and Meteorology faculty page for Benjamin M. Vallejo, Jr.
evidence.finding: The profile lists the 2011 barcode and 2014 and 2016 papers, but no 2010 proceedings entry in its recent-publication list. This non-exhaustive list does not resolve the citation.
The report says the 2010 National Research Symposium proceedings were produced and distributed, but does not provide an item-level table of contents or identify the Marikina contribution.

evidence.citation: NAST Transactions, volume 32, issue 1, abstract BS-39.
evidence.finding: The official NAST PDF contains the Marikina abstract on printed pages 80-81 under a distinct printed title. Its volume front matter says the NAST Annual Scientific Meeting was held 14-15 July 2010, which differs from the 2014 bibliography date of 10 July.

searchLimits.directCabiPage: HTTP 403; only indexed reference excerpt was available.
searchLimits.officialBarAndLibrarySearch: Exact-title and site searches of BAR/DA and UP/National Library-related domains did not surface an item-level BAR proceedings record or original full text.
searchLimits.conclusion: These were bounded web searches. No absence claim is made; an unindexed print or library copy may exist.

interpretation.citationPattern: The two 2011 Philippine Science Letters papers cite a 2010 BAR NRS proceedings entry titled with a Pterygoplichthys genus-level spelling and an Ondoy subtitle, pp. 1-15. The 2014 author-uploaded article and a CABI indexed excerpt cite a different title variant as NAST Transactions, vol. 32, p. 80. The official NAST volume contains a related Marikina abstract at pp. 80-81.
interpretation.assessment: The newer citations increase the possibility that the BAR wording is a misattribution, an alternate proceedings version, or a distinct contribution related to the NAST abstract. They do not establish which explanation is correct because the BAR primary item and its item-level contents remain unavailable.
interpretation.sampleDecision: No citation source gives a specimen or accession crosswalk among the two 2010 references, the 200-fish matrix-model sample, the 36-fish barcode series, the 2014 adults, or the 2016 five-station cohort. Do not infer overlap or independence.

evidenceDecision.decision: Retain the BAR citation as a separate bibliographic lead and link this follow-up as lower-confidence citation-context evidence. Keep its identity relative to NAST unresolved; no animal or occurrence record is supported.

nonClaims: A CABI indexed excerpt and an author-uploaded 2014 bibliography are secondary citation evidence, not the original BAR proceedings item.
The UP faculty publication list is non-exhaustive; its omission of the 2010 item does not show that the work was never published.
The date difference between the 2014 citation and the NAST volume front matter may be a citation error and does not prove a different event or sample.
No citation variant demonstrates a new survey, date, site, fish count, verified species identification, or present-day fish presence.
nextActions: Continue to use the official NAST abstract as the only directly retrieved 2010 proceedings text.
Treat the BAR proceedings volume as an unresolved archival retrieval lead; only revise the identity decision if its table of contents or primary contribution becomes available.
Keep all historical cohort counts separate unless specimen-level evidence links them.
